title: One Olive Branch, a Row of Bronze Statues: What the Ancient Olympics Really Looked Like
title_zh: 一顶橄榄枝，一排青铜像：古代奥运会究竟什么样
intro_zh: 本文约534词，含6个CET-4核心词（sacred, forbidden, spectators, competitors, penalty, endure），句子难度中等，适合四级阅读训练。

paragraphs.en: Imagine winning an Olympic gold medal today. It would follow you home, float in a bank vault, or shine in a museum. In ancient Olympia, a champion received something you could hold in one hand: a crown of sacred olive leaves, cut from a wild tree behind the temple of Zeus.
paragraphs.zh: 想象你今天赢得一枚奥运金牌。它会跟着你回家，躺进银行保险库，或者在博物馆里闪耀。而在古代奥林匹亚，冠军得到的东西一只手就能握住：一顶用神圣橄榄叶编成的花冠，叶子采自宙斯神庙后面的一棵野橄榄树。

paragraphs.en: The games began around 776 B.C. at Olympia, a quiet valley in southern Greece, and ran every four years for nearly twelve centuries. They were not a private hobby of athletes. They were a religious festival in honour of Zeus, the king of the gods, and the whole district fell silent for the weeks around them.
paragraphs.zh: 这项赛事大约始于公元前776年，地点是希腊南部一个安静的山谷——奥林匹亚，此后每四年举办一次，延续了近十二个世纪。它不是运动员的私人爱好，而是献给众神之王宙斯的宗教节庆，节庆前后那几周，整个地区都归于沉寂。

paragraphs.en: That silence was official. Before the games, messengers travelled across the Greek world announcing a truce. Wars stopped, roads opened, and weapons were forbidden inside the sanctuary. The truce did not end every war, but it made the roads safe enough for families to travel. Tens of thousands of spectators — traders, poets, politicians — made their way there, sleeping in tents or under the open sky.
paragraphs.zh: 这种沉寂是有官方效力的。赛会之前，使者走遍希腊世界宣布休战。战争停下，道路开放，任何人不得携带武器进入圣地。休战并不能终结每一场战争，但它让道路安全到普通家庭也敢上路。成千上万的观众——商人、诗人、政客——赶往那里，在帐篷里或露天过夜。

paragraphs.en: Only free Greek men could compete, and for a month beforehand competitors had to live in Olympia and train under official eyes. Married women were shut out completely: they could not watch, and any woman caught in the audience was thrown from a cliff. One mother who had trained her son in boxing slipped in dressed as a trainer, and was spared only because her family had produced so many champions. Girls, however, could run in a separate festival held for the goddess Hera.
paragraphs.zh: 只有自由出身的希腊男子才能参赛，而且赛前一个月，参赛者必须住在奥林匹亚，在官员的注视下训练。已婚妇女则完全被排除在外：她们不能观看，任何被发现混在观众中的女人都会被从悬崖上扔下去。有一位母亲曾亲自训练儿子练拳击，她装扮成教练混了进去，只因她家出过太多冠军才被饶恕。不过，女孩们可以参加另一个为女神赫拉举行的赛跑节。

paragraphs.en: The programme was short and hard. The stade race, a sprint of about 190 metres, gave the games their name; runners started from stone slabs whose grooves can still be seen today. Later came longer runs, wrestling, boxing, a pentathlon of five events, and finally chariot races, where rich men paid for the teams and the owners, not the drivers, took the prizes. The stadium held perhaps 45,000 people, and there were no seats: everyone stood on the earth banks in the August heat.
paragraphs.zh: 比赛项目简短而残酷。短跑“斯塔德”赛程约190米，运动会也因此得名；选手从石板起跑，石板上的凹槽至今仍能看到。后来又增加了长跑、摔跤、拳击、五项全能，最后是战车赛——富人们出钱组队，领奖的是马主而不是驭手。体育场大约能容纳四万五千人，却没有座位：所有人都站在土坡上，忍受八月的酷热。

paragraphs.en: Cheating was expensive. Athletes who bribed judges or broke the rules faced a penalty paid in silver, and the money was used to build bronze statues of Zeus beside the entrance to the stadium. Each base carried the offender's name, so every visitor walking in read who had shamed the games. More than a dozen such statues once stood in a row.
paragraphs.zh: 作弊的代价高昂。贿赂裁判或违规的运动员要缴纳一笔白银罚款，这笔钱被用来在体育场入口旁铸造宙斯青铜像。每座基座上都刻着违规者的名字，于是每个走进来的观众都能读到是谁给赛会抹了黑。这样的雕像曾一排立着十几座。

paragraphs.en: What the sports demanded most was the ability to endure pain. Boxing had no weight classes and no rounds: two men simply hit each other until one gave up, and broken noses were so common that the crowd expected them. A fighter named Arrhichion, so the story goes, won his last match by dying in it — his opponent surrendered first.
paragraphs.zh: 这些项目最考验的是忍受痛苦的能力。拳击不分体重级别，也不分回合：两个人就这么互相打，直到有一方认输，鼻子被打断太常见了，观众甚至习以为常。传说有一位名叫阿里基翁的拳手，是在比赛中死去才赢下最后一战的——他的对手先认了输。

paragraphs.en: In A.D. 393 the games were stopped for good, and the site was later buried by earthquakes and rivers. Yet the idea survived. The modern Olympics, which began in 1896, borrowed the four-year rhythm and much of the ceremony. Today a flame is lit among the ruins of Olympia and carried away in a relay, a custom invented in 1936. The prize has changed, but the honour of being watched by a whole city has not.
paragraphs.zh: 公元393年，这届赛会被永久叫停，此后遗址又被地震和河流掩埋。但这个理念活了下来。始于1896年的现代奥运会借用了四年一届的节奏和大部分仪式。今天，人们仍在奥林匹亚的废墟间点燃火种，再用接力把它带走——这一习俗源于1936年。奖品变了，但被整座城注视的那份荣誉没有变。

questions.q: Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?
options: Modern athletes earn far more money than ancient Greek athletes did.
The ancient Olympics were a religious festival with strict rules about who could take part and how.
The Greeks were the first people to invent chariot racing.
Ancient stadiums had no seats because wood was too expensive.
questions.explain: 全文围绕古代奥运会的性质（祭祀宙斯的宗教节庆）、参赛资格、项目、作弊处罚和观众条件展开，B概括最全面。A、C、D或为文中未提，或为局部细节。

questions.q: What happened to athletes who cheated at Olympia?
options: They were banned from the games for life.
They had to apologize to Zeus in public.
Their fine was used to make bronze statues of Zeus bearing their names.
They lost the prizes they had won at the previous games.
questions.explain: 第六段明确说明：违规者缴纳白银罚款，罚款被用来铸造宙斯青铜像，基座上刻着违规者的名字。A、B、D在文中均无依据。

questions.q: What can be inferred about married women in ancient Olympia?
options: They could watch the games but never take part.
They were kept out of the stadium completely.
They were sometimes allowed to act as trainers.
They could run in the festival held for Hera.
questions.explain: 第四段说已婚妇女不能观看，被发现混在观众中会被从悬崖扔下，可推断她们被完全挡在体育场之外。D是“女孩”可以参加的赫拉节，不是已婚妇女，属偷换概念。

questions.q: The word "endure" in Paragraph 7 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 第七段讲拳击没有回合、鼻梁常被打断，说明运动最考验的是忍受疼痛的能力，endure意为“忍受”，与bear最接近。
